surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the dissociation of the guanidinate ligand from the Ge(II) precursor by NH3, forming Ge-NH2 and guan-H. NH3 also reacts with the Te precursor to form TeH2, which then reacts with Ge-NH2 to form Ge-Te bonds. The process is self-limiting and involves the sequential dissociation and recombination of ligands on the surface.
evidence: The reaction mechanism was supported by ab initio calculations and detailed analysis of the reaction pathways. The text describes the dissociation of the guanidinate ligand from the Ge(II) precursor by NH3, the conversion of Te(SiMe3)2 to TeH2 by NH3, and the subsequent reaction between Ge-NH2 and TeH2 to form Ge-Te bonds. The reaction steps were analyzed using intrinsic reaction coordinates (IRC) and potential energy surface (PES) scans.
